Corrected 2026-07-14: rsid was corrupted (rs1053878 maps to chr9:136131651 GRCh37, the ABO gene locus - i.e. it was accidentally a duplicate-ish pointer to the OTHER ABO row, rs8176719) - replaced with rs590787, an RHD missense variant (Tyr311Ser/Cys), confirmed within RHD (chr1:25,598,884-25,656,936 GRCh37; row position chr1:25,629,943 falls inside the gene body). QC 2026-07-14 (H2): the only documented phenotype association found for this SNP is distinguishing weak-D/DEL from RhD-negative in a Chinese cohort (Shi et al 2019, PMID 30950221) - a narrow, population-specific question, NOT the standard RhD+/RhD- classification used in most clinical/consumer contexts (in Europeans, RhD-negative is usually caused by full RHD gene deletion, which a single coding SNP cannot detect). No general-population source was found confirming the G/G-vs-other genotype->RhD+/- direction assumed here. The previously-cited PMID 18403018 is an unrelated paper (Delphi-study methodology, not genetics) and has been removed rather than left as a false citation. Evidence downgraded B->D and weight halved; treat this row as low-confidence/exploratory only, NOT a reliable predictor of RhD status, until a validated RhD genotyping approach (e.g. deletion/CNV-based) is used instead.

Table 2 of Willcox 2008 directly genotyped rs13217795 and found G is the minor, longevity-associated allele (MAF 0.340 in long-lived cases vs 0.248 in average-lived controls, P=0.0006; G/G carriers had markedly lower insulin/HOMA-IR) - this confirms the effect_allele=G/risk_genotype=G/G/direction='+' already in this row.
